title: Regulation of Imports and Exports (Amendment) Bill
what_it_is: Regulation of Imports and Exports (Amendment) Bill

sections.label: Trade Information Certificates and Customs powers
sections.summary: The Bill strengthens regulation of Trade Information Certificates and facilitates Singapore Customs' investigative powers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: First, the Bill will strengthen our regulatory framework for the issuance of Trade Information Certificates (TICs).

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: Second, it will facilitate Singapore Customs' investigative powers to uphold the integrity of Singapore's trade regime.

sections.label: Expanded search warrant scope
sections.summary: Clause 10 expands search warrant scope to premises with other evidence of potential offences under the Act.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: Clause 10 of the Bill expands the scope for granting a search warrant to include circumstances where Singapore Customs have reasonable proof that the premises contain other forms of evidence related to the potential offence under this Act.

sections.label: Trade Information Certificate concept introduced
sections.summary: The Bill introduces Trade Information Certificates covering origin, export, re-export and processing certificates; a logistics coordinator was fined in June 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The Bill introduces the concept of a Trade Information Certificate, covering certificates of origin, export, re-export and processing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In June 2025, a logistics coordinator in Singapore was fined for falsifying and tampering with Certificates of Origin.

sections.label: New offences for false trade information
sections.summary: The Bill creates offences for issuing or altering false trade information, with fines and imprisonment for repeat offenders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The Bill's new offences for issuing or altering false trade information, with fines and imprisonment for repeat offenders, provide real deterrence.

sections.label: Response to trade circumvention
sections.summary: The Bill responds to trade circumvention by regulating Origin and Non-Manipulation Certificates, creating a false certificate offence and mandating record-keeping.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Bill appears to be a response to the problem of trade circumvention, sometimes pejoratively referred to as "Southeast Asia washing", where traders exploit major global trading hubs, like Singapore, to circumvent foreign trade restrictions and tariffs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It tackles this by directly regulating Origin and Non-Manipulation Certificates, introducing a new offence for knowingly issuing false Trade Information Certificates and mandating strict record-keeping for preferential Certificates of Origin.

sections.label: Penalties may deter smaller firms
sections.summary: Penalties up to $100,000 for a first offence risk deterring smaller firms from complex preferential trade.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The severe penalties, reaching up to $100,000 for a first offence, risk deterring smaller firms from participating in complex preferential trade, which requires them to issue or obtain these high-liability certificates.

sections.label: Assistance for traders' compliance
sections.summary: The speaker urges targeted Government assistance, possibly expanding the Enterprise Development Grant, to help traders, especially SMEs, comply with the Bill's obligations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To mitigate these foreseen problems and ensure the Bill does not become an unintended barrier to trade, I urge the Government to provide robust, targeted assistance to traders to help them comply with the Bill's obligations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It could expand on the existing Enterprise Development Grant, specifically for technology adoption by SMEs related to this Bill's requirements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This funding could cover up to 80% of the cost of the adoption or upgrade of traders' Enterprise Resource Planning systems and specialised Document Management Systems to meet the new requirements under this Bill.

sections.label: Tiered enforcement framework for traders
sections.summary: The speaker says local traders need resources, systems and trained personnel, and calls for a tiered enforcement framework distinguishing genuine error from deliberate fraud.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: If Singapore is to champion ASEAN digitalisation and lead in digital trade infrastructure, we must first ensure our local traders have the necessary resources, systems and trained personnel to meet the highest standards of trade data integrity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It should be formalised as a clear, tiered enforcement framework designed to differentiate between genuine error and deliberate fraud.

sections.label: Penalties reserved for fraud tier
sections.summary: The full penalty regime, including severe statutory fines, must be reserved strictly for Tier 3 covering fraud or gross negligence involving knowing falsehoods or intent to evade duties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The full penalty regime, including the severe statutory fines, must be reserved strictly for Tier 3, which covers fraud or gross negligence, where the breach involves knowing falsehoods, deliberate tampering or clear intent to evade duties.

sections.label: Gerald Giam on empowering traders
sections.summary: The speaker notes that Gerald Giam spoke on empowering traders, especially smaller ones, through targeted assistance for new stipulations under the proposed legislation.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: My hon friend, Gerald Giam, has just spoken on the importance of further empowering traders, especially smaller ones, through targeted assistance, as they navigate the new stipulations that they would have to comply with resulting from this proposed legislation.

sections.label: Certificates and new offences
sections.summary: The passage covers Certificates of Origin and other certificates, new offences for false or misleading certificates, and powers to suspend or revoke certificate issuers' authorisation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
sentences.text: These include Certificates of Origin, certificates confirming manufacture or processing in Singapore and certificates confirming that goods have been transshipped or re-exported here.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
sentences.text: It also introduces new offences for issuing or using false or misleading certificates and empowers the Director-General of Customs to suspend or revoke authorisation from certificate issuers who fail to meet the required standards.

sections.label: Singapore 2024 trade figures
sections.summary: In 2024, Singapore's total trade in goods reached $1.29 trillion and exports were $674 billion, with re-exports making up more than half.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Just last year, in 2024, Singapore's total trade in goods reached $1.29 trillion and exports were $674 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Re-exports made up more than half of that figure.

sections.label: Trade documentation regulation and SME compliance
sections.summary: The Bill strengthens trade documentation regulation, raising SME compliance costs, so agencies should support businesses and limit document searches to when necessary.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The new Bill strengthens regulation of trade documentation and certificates, making our export documents more credible and preventing issues with false certificates and false declarations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
sentences.text: For SMEs, the new procedures will increase compliance costs and time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Hence, Government agencies should provide guidance and support, so businesses view compliance as an asset rather than a burden.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I would also like to suggest that searches of company documents or computers only be carried out when necessary to safeguard business operations and trust.

sections.label: Non-governmental certificate issuers
sections.summary: The amendment allows other non-governmental and private entities to apply to Singapore Customs to be authorised certificate issuers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: With the amendment, other non-governmental and private entities can now apply to Singapore Customs to be authorised certificate issuers.

sections.label: Fit and proper certificate issuers
sections.summary: Singapore Customs will authorise only an applicant deemed fit and proper to issue certificates.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: To this end, Singapore Customs will authorise only an applicant that is deemed "fit and proper" to issue certificates.

sections.label: Investigative powers over digital records
sections.summary: Investigators need powers to inspect digitally-stored records, while efforts balance effective investigations with minimising disruption to legitimate business activities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: As digitally-stored records can be moved or altered quite quickly, it is crucial to grant investigators the powers to inspect these devices to ensure that the investigations are effective and efficient.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: I want to assure Members that every effort will be made to strike a balance between effective investigations and minimising disruption to legitimate business activities, and these are the majority.

sections.label: Search warrants and Bill's two aims
sections.summary: Search warrant applications need reasonable proof of evidence on the premises, and the Bill strengthens certificate issuance regulation and Singapore Customs' investigative powers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: Where a search warrant is required, its application must be made on reasonable proof that the premises contain evidence relating to the offence.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: To conclude, I would like to reiterate that this amendment Bill will do two things: first, strengthens Singapore's regulatory framework for the issuance of Trade Information Certificates by authorised certificate issuers; second, strengthens Singapore Customs' investigative powers to uphold the integrity of our trade regime.
